name: Sergey Goncharov
headline:
From infrastructure.

intro: I turn complex infrastructure into products people can use. My work connects cloud platforms, Kubernetes and agentic AI with the architecture, security and economics to make them work in practice.
current: Group Technical Product Manager at Virtuozzo
aboutTitle:
An architect’s depth.
A product leader’s perspective.
about: My career has followed the stack: from servers, storage and networking at HP and HPE, through cloud architecture and product management at Red Hat, to Kubernetes platform strategy at Mirantis. Today, at Virtuozzo, I focus on cloud platforms and the infrastructure foundations for AI.

I work where engineering choices become product decisions. Who needs this? What will it cost to operate? Where are the trust boundaries? How does a prototype become something a customer can depend on? Those questions shape both my enterprise work and the independent projects I build.
I’m especially interested in bringing agents and local LLMs into existing environments while preserving control over execution, data access and operational responsibility.

interviewIntro: In a PM interview, I want to understand how someone gets from a user’s problem to a decision they can defend. This is the path I look for.

steps.name: Clarify the user
steps.description: Name one specific person and one specific problem. “People who use the app” is too broad.

steps.name: Anchor to the business
steps.description: Explain who benefits economically: where the idea makes money or saves it.

steps.name: Pick the right segment
steps.description: Choose a group with a real problem, enough scale and a reason for the company to care.

steps.name: Define success first
steps.description: Say how you would measure success before proposing a feature.

steps.name: Show the trade-offs
steps.description: Lay out the alternatives you considered and explain why you chose yours.

steps.name: Give the answer structure
steps.description: Take time to organize your reasoning. A quick answer is only useful if people can follow it.

steps.name: State your assumptions
steps.description: Make your assumptions explicit so the interviewer can follow and challenge your reasoning.

steps.name: Prioritize
steps.description: Rank ideas by impact relative to effort. Be clear about what you would leave out.

steps.name: Follow the user journey
steps.description: Locate the problem across the whole experience, beyond a single screen.

steps.name: Return to the goal
steps.description: Connect each choice to the success measure you set at the start.

steps.name: Go deep on one idea
steps.description: Develop one idea far enough to test its logic, costs and consequences.

steps.name: Summarize your decision
steps.description: State your recommendation and the reason for it, clearly and briefly.

growthTitle:
Build the judgment.
Extend the reach.
growthIntro: The PM skills I encourage people to develop, from framing a problem to improving how a team works. Each layer builds on the ones below. Select a layer to explore the practice.

growthLayers.name: Sound judgment
growthLayers.summary: Define the problem. Make the call.

practices.name: Problem definition
practices.description: Identify which problems are worth solving before someone assigns them to you.
practices.tip: Bring a clear problem framing to your next roadmap review, before discussing features.

practices.name: Judgment under ambiguity
practices.description: Make a reasoned call when there is no playbook or clear answer.
practices.tip: Record your rationale for a difficult decision: what you knew, what you assumed and why you chose that path. Use that record when discussing your growth.

growthLayers.name: Product direction
growthLayers.summary: Connect the work to its value.

practices.name: Business impact framing
practices.description: Connect features to revenue, retention or a strategic outcome.
practices.tip: Write the “so what” for each initiative you own in terms a CFO would understand.

practices.name: Proactive roadmapping
practices.description: Enter planning with a point of view on where to invest, beyond the current backlog.
practices.tip: Write a one-page investment thesis for your area before the next planning cycle.

practices.name: Scope expansion
practices.description: Make decisions that improve something beyond your own team or product surface.
practices.tip: Name one decision this quarter that changed something outside your direct ownership.

practices.name: Strategic altitude
practices.description: Connect your work to the decisions made one level above your current role.
practices.tip: Rewrite your last project update as a briefing for a VP. Explain the outcome, the trade-off and the decision needed.

practices.name: Influence without authority
practices.description: Help people across functions reach decisions without relying on formal authority.
practices.tip: Track when another team changes direction because of your input, and what made the input useful.

practices.name: Cross-functional credibility
practices.description: Build the kind of judgment that other teams seek out before important decisions.
practices.tip: Notice who outside your team asks for your view. If no one does, start by finding where your expertise could help them.

growthLayers.name: Stronger teams
growthLayers.summary: Make the work clear. Help others grow.

practices.name: Organization-level narrative
practices.description: Explain why your work matters to the company as a whole.
practices.tip: Describe your work in two sentences. Ask someone outside product management to repeat the point back to you.

practices.name: Raise the standard around you
practices.description: Help the PMs around you improve how they think, decide and deliver.
practices.tip: Ask whether your team ships better work because you are there. Identify one way to make that contribution more useful.
